subject: pearlfish
title: A Fish Lives Inside a Sea Cucumber's Rear End and Eats Its Organs

scenes.text: This fish lives inside another animal. It goes in backwards.
A sea cucumber breathes through its rear end. Every time it opens up for a breath, a slim, see-through pearlfish is waiting.
It slides in tail first, a fish as long as your hand, and settles inside the sea cucumber's body.
Some species just hide in there from predators. The parasitic ones eat the host from the inside, mostly its gonads and breathing organs.
The host does not die, but it may never reproduce again. One sea cucumber was found holding fifteen fish at once.
Some sea cucumbers grew teeth around the opening to keep them out. A smaller pearlfish evolved and gets in anyway.

description:
Pearlfish are slim, eel-like fish that live inside sea cucumbers. The host breathes through its anus, and the fish waits for it to open, then slides in tail first.
Some species only shelter there, but parasitic pearlfish feed on the host's internal organs, mainly the gonads and the respiratory tree, which can stop the sea cucumber reproducing without killing it. In 1975 a biologist found 15 pearlfish inside a single leopard sea cucumber, and some sea cucumbers have evolved anal teeth that still fail to keep smaller species out.
Is this the worst roommate in the ocean? Comment below.

first_comment: Sea cucumbers are not their only homes: different pearlfish species also move into starfish, clams and sea squirts. Which ocean parasite should we cover next?
